LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 3.1.1 LISTENING FOR COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.1: Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension, part of Strand 3 in Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do we ensure personal safety in school? 2.Why should we read oral texts?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify verbs from an oral text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. respond to questions from an oral passage for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate listening to oral texts for enjoyment.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify verbs from an oral text,

   Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. respond to questions from an oral passage for comprehension,

   Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate listening to oral texts for enjoyment.

   Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to an oral passage from a pre- recorded audio or resource person on the theme,

2. team up to list down verbs identified from the oral text,

3. complete sentences orally by filling in the gaps using verbs,

4. play ‘the guessing language game’

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to an oral passage from a pre- recorded audio or resource person on the theme,
2. team up to list down verbs identified from the oral text,
3. complete sentences orally by filling in the gaps using verbs,
4. play ‘the guessing language game’

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Listening for Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: This is enhanced as the learner explores views when completing sentences orally by

filling in the gaps using verbs.

• Self-efficacy: This is promoted as the learner shows defining personal skills as they share experiences about personal safety.

Values:
• Love: This is promoted as the learner portrays a caring attitude when working with peers to play the language guessing

game.

• Responsibility: This is enhanced as the learner takes up assigned roles when teaming up to list down verbs identified from

the oral text.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and security: This is promoted as the learner is exposed to content on personal safety.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate their learning to concepts on personal safety in Science and Technology.
